heading: Run the tests yourself
intro: In these tasks a round pusher pushes a block onto a marked goal pose without grasping it. Pick a program the Code-as-Policies (CaP) agent wrote and press Run. The server runs it for {n} freshly drawn episodes inside the world model and then in the environment. Try v5 (the version the agent submitted) and then v4 (its predecessor) to see the difference the world model caught.
world_sub: 276 lines of Python, fitted from a few real trials
real_sub: The simulator standing in for the real system
status_queued: Another run is in progress. Waiting for it to finish.
status_error: That run failed. Please try again.
anim_caption: Each animation replays the first episode of its batch. The two start positions differ because the world model draws its own start states. An episode succeeds when the block covers more than 95% of the goal outline within 300 steps.
chart_x: Success rate in the world model
note_sample: Each run draws {n} random episodes per side, so the numbers change from press to press and can differ from the recorded results.
note_scope: Only the two pushing tasks run live here. The other six tasks are in the article below and in the repository.
card_short_description: Run pushing programs in the world model and environment
card_body: An interactive companion to [World Models as Unit Tests](https://dongzhezheng.github.io/world-models-as-unit-tests/). Pick one of the programs the CaP agent wrote for the planar pushing tasks and run it inside the world model and in the environment, live on the server. Code and recorded results are in the [repository](https://github.com/DongzheZheng/world-models-as-unit-tests).
